title: Twilight director reacts to Robert Pattinson's Bond casting
excerpt:
Catherine Hardwicke was surprised by Pattinson's reported Bond casting.
She recalled his Twilight audition and a memorable scene.
body_md:
Catherine Hardwicke, who directed the original Twilight film, has shared her reaction to the reported casting of Robert Pattinson as James Bond. During an appearance on The Kyle Buchanan Show, the filmmaker described her surprise at learning that the actor she helped introduce to a worldwide audience would be taking on another iconic screen character.

Hardwicke explained that Pattinson's established fame and his involvement with The Batman had made her doubtful that the Bond producers would choose him. She had expected the franchise to favor someone less closely associated with an existing blockbuster property. The news therefore came as a considerable surprise.

Her reaction also prompted an amusing recollection of the original Twilight audition. Hardwicke remembered that Pattinson and Kristen Stewart had performed an intimate scene during their screen test on the same bed where she later heard the Bond news. Pattinson had fallen off the bed during that audition, making her own nearly similar reaction a particularly memorable coincidence.

Twilight fans have also rediscovered a moment from the 2008 film that now carries an unexpected connection to the spy franchise. Eric Yorkie discusses the school's Monte Carlo-themed prom and makes a reference to James Bond, after which the film cuts to Pattinson's Edward Cullen.

Hardwicke explained that the reference was inspired by Pattinson's appearance during filming. His stylish arrival in sunglasses reminded her of the sophisticated fictional secret agent, encouraging her to include the Bond reference in the scene. The exchange was not intended as a prediction, but fans have naturally embraced its new significance.

Pattinson's career has changed considerably since the Twilight films made him an international star. Projects including Good Time and The Lighthouse demonstrated his willingness to explore challenging independent material, while The Batman established his ability to lead another major commercial franchise. That combination gives his prospective interpretation of Bond an especially interesting context.

Hardwicke praised the actor's distinctive personality and willingness to depart from conventional expectations. Her comments emphasize qualities she recognized during their earlier collaboration rather than offering details about how the new Bond film will approach the character.

The retrieved report does not establish a theatrical release date, plot synopsis or production schedule for the next James Bond movie. Accordingly, the filmmaker's reaction is best understood as a personal response to the casting report and a reflection on the actor's development since Twilight, rather than an announcement of additional production details.
